quote: Any girl can be glamorous. All you have to do is stand still and look stupid.

answer.name: Hedy Lamarr
answer.alias: The 1940s screen siren who co-invented frequency hopping

source: Quoted in Richard Schickel, The Stars (1962)
note: Her 1942 frequency-hopping patent underpins Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and GPS.

quote: I think Machiavelli's the most sophisticated writer outside of Shakespeare.
source: Interview, The Telegraph, c. 2002
note: He discovered the classics in prison. The Prince is still his favourite.

quote: I used to act dumb. It was an act. I am 26 years old, and that act is no longer cute.
source: Post-jail TV interview, June 2007 (ABC News)
note: Said three days after leaving the Los Angeles County jail.

quote: Science is humble. It knows what it knows and it knows what it doesn't know.
source: Essay 'Why I'm an Atheist', Wall Street Journal, 2010

quote: I find enough mystery in mathematics to satisfy my spiritual needs.

answer.name: Tom Lehrer
answer.alias: The guy who wrote 'Poisoning Pigeons in the Park'

source: Interview, June 1996
note: He taught maths at Harvard, MIT and UC Santa Cruz between satirical albums.

quote: I say there is more stupidity than hydrogen, and that is the basic building block of the universe.
source: The Real Frank Zappa Book (1989), p. 239
note: Not to be confused with Harlan Ellison's 'hydrogen and stupidity' line.

quote: My pleasures are the most intense known to man: writing and butterfly hunting.
source: Strong Opinions (1973), Foreword
note: His 1945 theory of blue-butterfly migration was confirmed by DNA sequencing in 2011.

quote: Let the credulous and the vulgar continue to believe that all mental woes can be cured by a daily application of old Greek myths to their private parts.
source: Strong Opinions (1973), p. 66
note: On Freud. He also called him 'the Viennese quack'.

quote: ...science is just pure empiricism, and by virtue of its method, it excludes metaphysics.
source: Comedy album A Wild and Crazy Guy (1978)
note: He majored in philosophy at Long Beach State before switching to comedy.

quote: Anyone who thinks the Large Hadron Collider will destroy the world is a twat.

answer.name: Brian Cox
answer.alias: Keyboard player of 90s pop band D:Ream

source: Radio Times interview, 8 September 2008
note: He left the band for a PhD in particle physics and worked on the LHC.

quote: If you want to inspire confidence, give plenty of statistics – it does not matter that they should be accurate, or even intelligible, so long as there is enough of them.

answer.name: Lewis Carroll
answer.alias: The guy who wrote Alice in Wonderland

source: Three Years in a Curatorship (1886)
note: Charles Dodgson, Oxford maths lecturer, on running the Christ Church Common Room.

quote: ...He cannot bury his mistakes in the grave like the doctors. He cannot argue them into thin air or blame the judge like the lawyers.

answer.name: Herbert Hoover
answer.alias: The US President who was a mining engineer

source: The Memoirs of Herbert Hoover, Vol. 1 (1951), ch. 11
note: On the engineer. Hoover also translated a 1556 Latin mining treatise with his wife.

quote: It converts its RNA into DNA and then it gets into your nucleus, and it inserts itself into your DNA

answer.name: Dexter Holland
answer.alias: Lead singer of The Offspring

source: Men's Health interview, 2024 (via Louder)
note: On HIV. He has a PhD in molecular biology from USC; his thesis was on HIV microRNA.

quote: I have great hope and faith, but it's a humanistic faith based in facts; you have to believe that facts exist.

answer.name: Greg Graffin
answer.alias: Lead singer of Bad Religion

source: Discover magazine interview, 6 October 2010
note: He has a PhD in zoology from Cornell and lectures on evolution at UCLA.

quote: We're interested in zodiacal dust because, presumably, the dust has a lot to say about the way planetary systems evolved

answer.name: Brian May
answer.alias: Lead guitarist of Queen

source: Imperial College alumni lecture, 14 November 2007
note: He finished his astrophysics PhD in 2007, 36 years after starting it.

quote: ...we have unwittingly begun a massive experiment with the system of this planet itself...
source: Speech to the Royal Society, 27 September 1988
note: On greenhouse gases. She was a research chemist before politics.

quote: Please excuse my not mailing this — but I don't know your new address.
source: P.S. of a letter to his late wife Arline, 17 October 1946
note: Arline died of TB 16 months earlier. The letter stayed sealed until his death in 1988.

quote: Hell, if I could explain it to the average person, it wouldn't have been worth the Nobel prize.
source: Remark c. 1965, quoted in People magazine, 22 July 1985

quote: I'd hate to die twice. It's so boring.
source: Last words, 15 February 1988 (James Gleick, Genius, 1992)

quote: Women. They are a complete mystery.
source: New Scientist interview at 70, 4 January 2012
note: His answer to 'What do you think about most during the day?'

quote: If aliens visit us, the outcome would be much as when Columbus landed in America, which didn't turn out well for the Native Americans.
source: Into the Universe with Stephen Hawking, Discovery Channel, 2010

quote: Even on the most solemn occasions I got away without wearing socks and hid that lack of civilisation in high boots.
source: Letter to his cousin Elsa, quoted in New Scientist, 15 July 2006
note: He later married her.

quote: Why is it nobody understands me and everybody likes me?
source: New York Times, 'The Einstein Theory of Living', 12 March 1944

quote: The theory is like a beggar clothed in purple whom ignorant people take for a king.
source: New York Times, 11 July 1935 (79th birthday press conference)
note: On Einstein's relativity, which he called 'a mass of error'.

quote: This growing tendency of women to overshadow the masculine is a sign of a deteriorating civilization.
source: Galveston Daily News, 10 August 1924
note: From an interview titled 'Mr. Tesla Explains Why He Will Never Marry'.

quote: Threatning my father and mother Smith to burne them and the house over them
source: Coded list of sins, Fitzwilliam notebook, 1662
note: Sin no. 13 of 57, written at age 19. No. 24 is 'Punching my sister'.

quote: It may end later, but I see no reason for its ending sooner.
source: Manuscript on the Book of Daniel, c. 1704 (Yahuda collection)
note: On the world, which he calculated would end no earlier than 2060.

quote: I hate a Barnacle as no man ever did before, not even a Sailor in a slow-sailing ship.
source: Letter to W. D. Fox, 24 October 1852
note: He spent eight years classifying barnacles.

quote: The sight of a feather in a peacock's tail, whenever I gaze at it, makes me sick!
source: Letter to Asa Gray, 3 April 1860
note: It was a thorn in natural selection's side until he thought up sexual selection.

quote: Only picture to yourself a nice soft wife on a sofa with good fire, & books & music perhaps
source: 'This is the Question: Marry / Not Marry' memorandum, July 1838
note: From a pros-and-cons list. Conclusion: 'Marry — Marry — Marry Q.E.D.'

quote: I was taught at school never to start a sentence without knowing the end of it.

answer.name: Paul Dirac
answer.alias: The Nobel physicist who predicted antimatter

source: Quoted in Michael Berry, 'The purest soul in physics', Physics World, 1998
note: Cambridge colleagues defined a unit, the 'dirac': one word per hour.

quote: In science one tries to tell people, in such a way as to be understood by everyone, something that no one ever knew before. But in the case of poetry, it's the exact opposite!

answer.name: Paul Dirac
answer.alias: The Nobel physicist who predicted antimatter

source: Quoted in Robert Jungk, Brighter Than a Thousand Suns (1958)
note: Said to Oppenheimer, who wrote poetry on the side.

quote: Science is a differential equation. Religion is a boundary condition.
source: Epigram sent to Robin Gandy, 1954

quote: It's not even probable, let alone scientifically proven, that HIV causes AIDS.

answer.name: Kary Mullis
answer.alias: The guy who invented PCR

source: Spin magazine, Vol. 10 No. 4, 1994
note: Nobel Prize in Chemistry, 1993. PCR is the technique behind most HIV tests.

quote: I think I think harder, think more than other people do, than other scientists.

answer.name: Linus Pauling
answer.alias: The only person with two unshared Nobel Prizes

source: Interview, Big Sur, 11 November 1990
note: He also spent his last decades insisting vitamin C cures cancer.

quote: These developments may lead to an explanation of processes still not understood within conventional science such as telepathy, an area where Britain is at the forefront of research.

answer.name: Brian Josephson
answer.alias: Nobel physicist with a quantum 'junction' named after him

source: Royal Mail Nobel centenary stamp booklet, October 2001
note: Written for the Royal Mail. Oxford physicist David Deutsch called it 'utter rubbish'.

quote: People say it would be terrible if we made all girls pretty. I think it would be great.

answer.name: James Watson
answer.alias: The guy who co-discovered the structure of DNA

source: Documentary DNA, reported in New Scientist, 28 February 2003
note: Nobel Prize, 1962. His lab eventually cut all ties with him.

quote: Bin Laden has won, in airports of the world every day. I had a little jar of honey, now thrown away by rule-bound dundridges. STUPID waste.
source: Tweet, 3 November 2013
note: 'Dundridge' is his own coinage for a petty rule-enforcer. Twitter named it #honeygate.

quote: I can think of no moral objection to eating human road kills.
source: To Peter Singer, The Genius of Charles Darwin: Uncut Interviews (2009)

quote: Not that anybody's asked, but New Years Day on the Gregorian Calendar is a cosmically arbitrary event, carrying no Astronomical significance at all.
source: Tweet, 1 January 2018
note: Posted at the start of New Year's Day.

quote: The illegality of cannabis is outrageous, an impediment to full utilization of a drug which helps produce the serenity and insight, sensitivity and fellowship so desperately needed in this increasingly mad and dangerous world.
source: Essay as 'Mr. X' (1969), in Lester Grinspoon, Marihuana Reconsidered (1971)
note: Published under a pseudonym. Grinspoon revealed the author after Sagan's death.

quote: ...the physicists have known sin; and this is a knowledge which they cannot lose.

answer.name: J. Robert Oppenheimer
answer.alias: The father of the atomic bomb

source: Arthur D. Little Memorial Lecture, MIT, 25 November 1947

quote: I adopted the theory of Reincarnation when I was twenty six.

answer.name: Henry Ford
answer.alias: The Model T guy

source: San Francisco Examiner interview, 26 August 1928
note: He also said 'History is more or less bunk.'

quote: ...anyone who is looking for a source of cheap power in the transformation of the atom, is talking pure moonshine.

answer.name: Ernest Rutherford
answer.alias: The guy who split the atom

source: Calgary Daily Herald, 7 October 1933
note: Twelve years before Hiroshima.

quote: The more important fundamental laws and facts of physical science have all been discovered...

answer.name: Albert A. Michelson
answer.alias: The guy who measured the speed of light

source: Light Waves and Their Uses (1903), pp. 23–25
note: Two years later Einstein published special relativity. Michelson won the Nobel in 1907.

quote: I have not the smallest molecule of faith in aerial navigation other than ballooning...

answer.name: Lord Kelvin
answer.alias: The guy the temperature scale is named after

source: Letter declining to join the Aeronautical Society, 8 December 1896
note: Seven years before Kitty Hawk.

quote: ...in 1901 I said to my brother Orville that man would not fly for fifty years. Two years later we ourselves made flights.

answer.name: Wilbur Wright
answer.alias: The guy who invented the airplane

source: Speech to the Aéro-Club de France, Paris, 5 November 1908
note: He added that the shock had made him distrust all his own predictions since.

quote: I am bold enough to say that such a man-made voyage will never occur regardless of all future advances.

answer.name: Lee de Forest
answer.alias: The father of radio

source: Associated Press interview, 25 February 1957
note: On landing a man on the Moon, 'a wild dream worthy of Jules Verne'. Apollo 11: 1969.

quote: The baby of the twenty-first century will be rocked in a steel cradle; his father will sit in a steel chair...

answer.name: Thomas Edison
answer.alias: The light bulb guy

source: Interview, Miami Metropolis, 1911
note: He also predicted ocean liners made of solid gold.

quote: It's utter bilge. I don't think anybody will ever put up enough money to do such a thing . . . What good would it do us?

answer.name: Richard Woolley
answer.alias: Britain's Astronomer Royal, 1956

source: Time magazine, 16 January 1956
note: On space travel. Sputnik launched 21 months later.

quote: The influence of coffee in stimulating the genital organs is notorious.

answer.name: John Harvey Kellogg
answer.alias: The cornflakes guy

source: Plain Facts for Old and Young (1881), pp. 391–393
note: His bland diet was meant to dampen the passions. Corn flakes came out of it.

quote: Males have more teeth than females in the case of men, sheep, goats, and swine; in the case of other animals observations have not yet been made.
source: History of Animals, Book II, Part 3 (c. 350 BC), trans. D'Arcy Thompson
note: He was married twice and apparently never counted.

quote: The most inexcusable and disgraceful of all noises is the cracking of whips...
source: 'On Noise', Parerga and Paralipomena (1851), trans. T. Bailey Saunders
note: He proposed that whip-crackers receive 'five really good blows with a stick'.

quote: America is a mistake, admittedly a gigantic mistake, but a mistake nevertheless.
source: Remark to Ernest Jones, in Jones's Life and Work of Sigmund Freud, vol. 2 (1955)
note: He visited once, in 1909, and blamed American food for his digestion forever after.

quote: In my last depression I took Coca again and a small dose lifted me to the heights in a wonderful fashion.
source: Letter to his fiancée Martha Bernays, 2 June 1884
note: He went on to publish 'Über Coca', a scientific love letter to the drug.

quote: I'm proud of my invention, but I'm sad that it is used by terrorists... I would prefer to have invented a machine that people could use and that would help farmers with their work — for example a lawnmower.

answer.name: Mikhail Kalashnikov
answer.alias: The guy who invented the AK-47

source: Interview, The Guardian, 29 July 2002
note: He always said he had wanted to build farm machinery.

quote: There is no form of prose more difficult to understand and more tedious to read than the average scientific paper.

answer.name: Francis Crick
answer.alias: The other guy who co-discovered the structure of DNA

source: The Astonishing Hypothesis (1994)

quote: To ask a politician to lead us is to ask the tail of a dog to lead the dog.

answer.name: Buckminster Fuller
answer.alias: The geodesic dome guy

source: 'The Designers and the Politicians' (1962)
note: He also wanted to put all the world's politicians in a rocket to the Moon.

quote: Perchance you who pronounce my sentence are in greater fear than I who receive it.

answer.name: Giordano Bruno
answer.alias: The friar burned at the stake for saying the stars are other suns

source: To his judges at sentencing, 8 February 1600 (reported by Kaspar Schoppe)
note: He was burned in Rome's Campo de' Fiori nine days later.

quote: The SF created us to enjoy our suffering.

answer.name: Paul Erdős
answer.alias: The most prolific mathematician of the 20th century

source: Quoted in Paul Hoffman, The Man Who Loved Only Numbers (1998), p. 4
note: SF = 'Supreme Fascist', his name for God, who hid his glasses and stole his passport.
